passages.title: How Plants Make Food
paragraphs: You get energy from the food you eat. But have you ever wondered what plants eat? Plants cannot walk to a kitchen or hunt for a snack. Instead, they make their own food in an amazing process called photosynthesis.
The word photosynthesis comes from two Greek words: "photo," meaning light, and "synthesis," meaning putting together. So photosynthesis means putting things together using light.

To make food, a plant needs three ingredients. First, its roots take in water from the soil. Second, tiny holes in its leaves, called stomata, take in a gas from the air called carbon dioxide. Third, its leaves catch energy from sunlight.

Leaves are green because they contain chlorophyll. Chlorophyll is a green substance that traps the Sun's energy. The plant uses this energy to turn water and carbon dioxide into a kind of sugar called glucose. This sugar is the plant's food, and it helps the plant grow.
Photosynthesis also makes oxygen, which the plant releases into the air. Every time you breathe in, you are using oxygen that plants helped make. So the next time you see a tree, say thank you!

questions.prompt: What does the Greek word "photo" mean?
What three things does a plant need to make food?
What is the green substance in leaves that traps the Sun's energy?
What gas does photosynthesis release into the air?
Why does the writer say we should thank trees?
options: Because trees keep the rain away
Because trees help make the oxygen we breathe

passages.title: The Great Wall of China
paragraphs: Imagine a wall so long that it would take you well over a year to walk from one end to the other. That wall is real! It is the Great Wall of China, one of the most famous structures on Earth.

The Great Wall is not just one wall. It is a long chain of walls, towers and forts built over more than 2,000 years. Different rulers of China kept building, repairing and joining the walls. Most of the parts that tourists visit today were built during the Ming dynasty, hundreds of years ago.

Why build such a giant wall? Its main job was protection. The walls helped keep out attackers from the north and let soldiers guard the borders. Guards in the watchtowers could send warning signals using smoke during the day and fire at night.
Building the wall was very hard work. Soldiers, farmers and prisoners carried stone, brick and earth up steep mountains, often in freezing cold or burning heat.

Some people say you can see the Great Wall from space with just your eyes, but that is a myth. The wall is very long, but it is too narrow to spot from that far away. Today it is a World Heritage Site that millions of people visit every year.

questions.prompt: What was the main job of the Great Wall?
options: To be a road for traders

questions.prompt: During which dynasty were most of the parts that tourists visit today built?
How did guards send warnings at night?
The text says seeing the wall from space is a "myth." What does myth mean here?
options: Something many people believe that is not true

questions.prompt: Why do you think the watchtowers were important?
options: Guards could see attackers coming and warn others

passages.title: The Emperor's Seeds
paragraphs: Long ago, a wise emperor was growing old. He had no children, so he needed to choose someone to rule the kingdom after him. He came up with a clever plan.
The emperor called all the children of the kingdom to the palace and gave each child one seed. "Plant this seed and care for it," he said. "Come back in one year and show me what you have grown."

A girl named Lin planted her seed in a pot of rich soil. She watered it every day and kept it in the sunshine. Weeks passed, then months, but nothing grew. She moved it to a bigger pot with better soil. Still, nothing grew.

When the year ended, the other children marched to the palace carrying beautiful plants and bright flowers. Lin felt ashamed of her empty pot. Her father said, "You did your best, and that is enough. Be honest."

The emperor looked at every plant without smiling. When he reached Lin, he asked, "Why is your pot empty?" With tears in her eyes, Lin told him the truth. The emperor smiled. "I cooked all the seeds before I gave them out," he said. "None of them could grow. The others swapped their seeds for new ones. Only you were brave enough to be honest. You will be the next ruler."

questions.prompt: Why did the emperor need to choose someone?
options: He had no children to rule after him
He was moving to another kingdom

questions.prompt: What did Lin do when her seed did not grow at first?
options: She moved it to a bigger pot with better soil

questions.prompt: What had the emperor done to all the seeds?
questions.answerText: He cooked them so they could not grow

questions.prompt: Why did the other children have beautiful plants?
What is the main lesson of the story?
options: Honesty takes courage, and it is worth it
